drivers.detail: 1/10/2026 adjustment: E10 RON95 +100 to 27,180 VND/l; E5 RON92 +170 to 26,560; diesel -780 to 29,710; mazut up. In September petrol rose 9.39% m/m and diesel 4.53%; transport +3.97% m/m, adding 0.4pp to CPI.
Brent +4.4% to $102.31/bbl on 1/10/2026 (US sending third carrier group to Middle East); upside risk to the mid-Oct and later fuel adjustments.
EIA: Brent about $90/b in 2H26, $91 2026 avg, falling to ~$77 by 2Q27, $74 2027 avg as Hormuz constraints ease and inventories rebuild.

Average retail tariff unchanged since 10/5/2025 (2,204.07 VND/kWh). Decree 278/2026 (effective 9/7/2026) allows changes every 3 months: <2% rise or <1% cut means no change; 2-<5% rises need MOIT opinion. EVN made >12,200bn VND profit in 8M/2026. Press asks whether a cut is possible; MoF says timing and scope of electricity, health and education price changes must be weighed against inflation. No adjustment announced as of early Oct. Sept electricity CPI -0.13%.

Education +1.41% m/m in Sept 2026 (+0.08pp), as private schools and universities raised fees. University fee ceilings for 2026-27 rise ~190-350k VND/month (vocational ~150-250k) under the Decree 97/2023 roadmap. Effect lands mainly in Sept; no source quantifies any October spillover.

No specific Q4-2026 price decision found. On 4/9/2026 MoF asked MoH to set a roadmap for medical service prices 'aligned with inflation control targets'. Healthcare CPI +0.24% m/m in Sept. Treat as upside risk, not a scheduled change.
Live hog prices fell across all regions in late Sept to 56-59k VND/kg, losing the 60k level.
Domestic raw rice broadly stable (CL555/IR504 +50 VND/kg) as autumn-winter harvest arrives. FAO world rice index +1.4% in Sept 2026.

NSO USD index -0.69% m/m and -1.34% y/y in Sept. SBV central rate 25,630 on 30/9. VNDirect expects USD/VND stable around 26,000 at end-2026 (20/9). UOB sees 26,400 in Q4-26 and 26,100 in Q2-27 (June). MBS sees 26,800-27,000 at end-2026 (July). Low imported-inflation pressure from FX for now.
MoF/Steering Committee: public investment, year-end consumption and infrastructure projects lift demand for construction materials, fuel and raw materials in the last months of 2026.

The 2pp VAT cut (10% to 8%) is set to end 31/12/2026, with goods reverting to 10% from 1/1/2027 unless extended. OECD (June 2026) expects the 'planned VAT rate increase at the beginning of 2027' to keep inflation elevated.

drivers.detail: Own arithmetic, not a published forecast. From Sept yoy 5.08: flat m/m in Q4 gives Oct/Nov/Dec yoy 4.87/4.40/4.20 and a 2026 avg ~4.51. +0.2% m/m gives 5.08/4.82/4.83, avg ~4.62. +0.4% m/m gives 5.29/5.24/5.46, avg ~4.72.
